headline: Engineering services pipeline healthy and booked revenue growing; increasing focus on defense tech intellectual property and sovereign capability plays, with ambition to move beyond services revenue toward product and IP licensing
reasoning: Beyond the cardiac AI deal, Hydrix's engineering services business has booked significant contracted revenue and maintains a healthy pipeline. The company has increased its focus on defense technology opportunities, particularly around building intellectual property in sovereign defense tech, working with defense-focused clients under government agency mandates. Management is seeking to translate research through universities, clients and agencies into commercialised defense tech products that go beyond pure services revenue — analogous to the product revenue model achieved in the medical segment. Coote suggests the market cap does not yet reflect the product/IP potential, and that execution on contract sales and IP licensing deals will be the key re-rating catalyst.
quote: The engineering services business has booked a lot of contracted revenue recently, continues to maintain and progress a very, very healthy pipeline. And as we've announced in the June quarter, the increased focus around the defense tech opportunities and the pursuit around a building, a position in intellectual property, in defense technology, off the back of our sovereign capability... I think investors should continue to watch what we can, what we get to do here in the defense tech space, as I said, around intellectual property, so that we can move beyond just the service's revenue generating business and do more deals like medical, which is a product revenue based play.
episode_title: Hydrix’s cardiac AI gets a Singapore launchpad

headline: First contract sale for cardiac AI platform (Simplicity) with Singapore's NHC — a top 10-15 global cardiac centre — generating ~$200k/year revenue, with December quarter start expected and multiple other Singapore and Australian hospital conversations ongoing
reasoning: Hydrix has secured a multi-year contract with a leading Singapore cardiac centre (NHC) for its Simplicity cardiac AI platform, which the company has held distribution rights to for several years. The deal took 2-3 years to complete due to IT security and patient privacy compliance hurdles. Revenue of a few hundred thousand dollars per year is expected to flow from the December quarter, with a ~90-day cloud-based implementation. The platform is OEM-agnostic, consolidating all cardiac implantable electronic device monitoring into one AI-enabled screen, with healthy gross margins on a per-patient pricing model. The Singapore reference account is expected to accelerate procurement conversations with other cardiac centres in Singapore and Australia.
quote: It's the first contract sale that we've achieved with simplicity. We've had the rights to distribute that product for the last several years, and the contract has taken literally the last 2 to 3 years to work with the hospital, build confidence, prove that the IT security around patient privacy, etc. and all those sorts of really important boxes can be ticked. Creates a reference account for the region, Australia, Singapore and beyond. And it's all about AI enabled cardiac care at the end of the day.
episode_title: Hydrix’s cardiac AI gets a Singapore launchpad
